_: GOLDEN FIXTURES for prlint.parse_pr_body, captured from the PYTHON implementation on 2026-10-14.
WHY THEY EXIST: `prlint` is 1,133 lines with 22 problem sites in ONE function, and its body
parser is the shared input to every gate. `parity.py` - the most valuable verification in this
port - DIES WITH PYTHON, so capturing behaviour as data is the only safety net that survives it.
A port checked against these cannot silently drift while claiming agreement.
WHAT THE CAPTURE ALREADY EXPOSED, which reading the parser did not: `line_of` is set on the RAW
TEMPLATE, where `line_count` is not; `milestone_ref` is set in cases that name no milestone; and
`empty` still produces `headline_before`/`headline_after` objects rather than nothing. THOSE ARE
THE CASES A PORT WRITTEN FROM THE DOCSTRING WOULD GET WRONG.
`expected` was produced by calling the Python parser; it is a RECORD OF BEHAVIOUR, not a
specification. Where a value looks wrong, the fixture is still right and the PORT must match it
until someone decides to change the behaviour deliberately.
Regenerate: run the capture in docs/labs/prlint-fixtures-2026-10-14/README.md against Python.

`body_text` AND `raw` ARE RECORDED NOW, and they are not decoration: `_find_milestone` scores candidate milestones partly on `body_text`, so without it the milestone the body is ABOUT cannot be identified and the registry-dependent gates cannot be ported at all. THEY LOOKED LIKE PARSER INTERNALS until a gate needed them - which is why the fixtures record what the PARSER RETURNS rather than the fields that seemed interesting at the time.
